cause.what_happened: A -6.3% day to the 15:05 ET screen, split between a -3.4% gap and -3.0% intraday, on 1.03x normal volume. It follows -8.96% on 10-06. There is no 8-K, Form 4 or prospectus filed 10-06 or 10-07, so the most likely driver is the Solana price this treasury company holds. I could not source today's SOL move, so that cause is an inference, not a sourced fact.

evidence.claim: The latest 8-K is dated 10-05 (Items 2.02/8.01): 2,564,212 SOL and SOL equivalents as of 10-02, worth $302M per the release. That implies roughly $118 per SOL, so the equity is a leveraged SOL proxy.
The EDGAR atom feed shows no filing after 2026-10-05, so nothing company-specific was filed on the two drop days.

pipeline.next_dated_event: The next weekly SOL-holdings 8-K, on the Monday cadence of 09-14, 09-21, 09-28 and 10-05, would land about 2026-10-12, outside the window. Q3 results are estimated for 2026-11-17 (a Zacks estimate, not company-announced). Nothing dated falls inside the window.
pipeline.what_would_change_my_mind: An 8-K or 424B5 filed tonight showing common ATM sales, a buyback authorisation, or a large SOL-denominated borrowing change; or a sourced Solana move of several percent overnight.

findings.finding: The common-stock ATM prospectus supplement (424B5, 2026-06-01) is still on file, and a $300M CHAD preferred ATM was added in September. Either could sell into the window, but only the common one dilutes the common directly.
findings.mechanism_in_window: An ATM sells daily without a new filing, so supply could land on 10-08 itself. I found no evidence of common ATM sales in the latest releases: the 10-05 release names only the CHAD ATM as growth capital. CHAD issuance is intended at or above its $10 stated amount and adds no common shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No dated common-ATM disclosure is matched to a reaction in the baseline. The stock's own 12 comparable falls since July split 5 up / 7 down next session, median about -0.9%.
findings.why_not_priced: The ATM is a standing overhang the price already knows about. What is unpriced is only whether the company chooses to sell common into a bounce. A treasury company trading near its SOL value usually avoids selling common, because it cuts SOL per share. That is why this is small, and why I treat any bounce as capped rather than reversed.
findings.independence: The 09-21 8-K exhibit describes the $300M CHAD ATM (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1805526/000180552626000109/dfdv-exx991_92126.htm). It is preferred, not common, so it is only weakly the same direction.
